Player Profile

My Journey

My baseball journey has never been a straight line, and that's something I'm proud of.

I started my development at Inspiration Academy, attended Cardinal Mooney, and graduated from Lakewood Ranch High School during the COVID era. After high school, I earned a scholarship to Polk State College where I developed into one of the program's most reliable bullpen arms and earned Fireman of the Year honors in 2023.

At Polk State, I also learned to pitch from a submarine arm slot, adding another dimension to my game. My performance led me to the University of Tennessee, where competing in the SEC challenged me to grow as a player and person. I later transferred to UNC Charlotte to finish my collegiate career.

One of the biggest lessons I've learned is to focus on competing one pitch at a time instead of worrying about velocity, stats, or the scoreboard. That mindset has helped me grow the most.

My goal is to play professional baseball and eventually use the lessons and relationships from the game to build a successful business.

University of Tennessee

Competing in the SEC pushed me to improve every day and raised my standards as a competitor. Tennessee was a major step in my development and prepared me for the next chapter of my career.

Pitching Profile

Scouting Report

Combs offers a different look than a typical college right-hander. He can attack from multiple arm slots, change eye levels, and use his changeup shape to miss barrels and keep hitters from sitting on fastball timing.
